sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bṛhatīṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ dṛṣṭvā senāṃ samudyatām viṣādam agamad rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Beholding the vast army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons drawn up for battle, King Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, was overcome with dejection.

sanskrit: vyūhaṃ bhīṣmeṇa cābhedyaṃ kalpitaṃ prekṣya pāṇḍavaḥ abhedyam iva saṃprekṣya viṣaṇṇo 'rjunam abravīt
english: Seeing the impenetrable battle-array marshalled by Bhīṣma, and perceiving it to be as if unbreakable, the son of Pāṇḍu, downcast, spoke to Arjuna.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjaya kathaṃ śakyam asmābhir yoddhum āhave dhārtarāṣṭrair mahābāho yeṣāṃ yoddhā pitāmahaḥ
english: O Dhanaṃjaya, mighty-armed one, how shall we be able to fight in battle against the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, whose champion is the grandsire himself?

sanskrit: akṣobhyo 'yam abhedyaś ca bhīṣmeṇāmitrakarśinā kalpitaḥ śāstradṛṣṭena vidhinā bhūritejasā
english: This array, unshakable and impenetrable, has been formed by Bhīṣma, scourge of foes, of abundant splendour, according to the method ordained in the science of war.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ saṃśayaṃ prāptāḥ sasainyāḥ śatrukarśana katham asmān mahāvyūhād udyānaṃ no bhaviṣyati
english: We, with our troops, are plunged into doubt, O scourge of foes. How shall there be escape for us from this mighty array?

sanskrit: athārjuno 'bravīt pārthaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram amitrahā viṣaṇṇam abhisaṃprekṣya tava rājann anīkinīm
english: Then Arjuna, slayer of foes, looking upon the army of yours, O king, addressed the dejected son of Pṛthā, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: prajñayābhyadhikāñ śūrān guṇayuktān bahūn api jayanty alpatarā yena tan nibodha viśāṃ pate
english: By that means whereby the few overcome even the many heroes, men superior in wisdom and endowed with virtues—understand it, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: tat tu te kāraṇaṃ rājan pravakṣyāmy anasūyave nāradas tam ṛṣir veda bhīṣmadroṇau ca pāṇḍava
english: I shall declare to you that cause, O king, since you bear no malice. The sage Nārada knows it, and so do Bhīṣma and Droṇa, O son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: etam evārtham āśritya yuddhe devāsure 'bravīt pitāmahaḥ kila purā mahendrādīn divaukasaḥ
english: Resting upon this very truth, the Grandsire, long ago, in the war between the gods and the demons, spoke to the dwellers of heaven led by mighty Indra.

sanskrit: na tathā balavīryābhyāṃ vijayante jigīṣavaḥ yathā satyānṛśaṃsyābhyāṃ dharmeṇaivodyamena ca
english: Those who seek to conquer do not win victory so much by strength and prowess as by truth and compassion, by righteousness and by exertion.

sanskrit: tyaktvādharmaṃ ca lobhaṃ ca mohaṃ codyamam āsthitāḥ yudhyadhvam anahaṃkārā yato dharmas tato jayaḥ
english: Casting off unrighteousness, greed, and delusion, and taking your stand upon exertion, fight without arrogance; for where there is righteousness, there is victory.

sanskrit: evaṃ rājan vijānīhi dhruvo 'smākaṃ raṇe jayaḥ yathā me nāradaḥ prāha yataḥ kṛṣṇas tato jayaḥ
english: Know this, O king: certain is our victory in battle. For as Nārada has told me, where Kṛṣṇa is, there is victory.

sanskrit: guṇabhūto jayaḥ kṛṣṇe pṛṣṭhato 'nveti mādhavam anyathā vijayaś cāsya saṃnatiś cāparo guṇaḥ
english: Victory is an attribute inherent in Kṛṣṇa; it follows close behind Mādhava. And conquest is his besides, while humility is yet another of his virtues.

sanskrit: anantatejā govindaḥ śatrupūgeṣu nirvyathaḥ puruṣaḥ sanātanatamo yataḥ kṛṣṇas tato jayaḥ
english: Govinda, of boundless splendour, is untroubled amid hosts of enemies; he is the most ancient Person. Where Kṛṣṇa is, there is victory.

sanskrit: purā hy eṣa harir bhūtvā vaikuṇṭho 'kuṇṭhasāyakaḥ surāsurān avasphūrjann abravīt ke jayantv iti
english: For of old, becoming Hari, the dweller in Vaikuṇṭha, whose shafts are never blunted, thundering forth amid gods and demons, he asked: 'Who shall be victorious?'

sanskrit: anu kṛṣṇaṃ jayemeti yair uktaṃ tatra tair jitam tatprasādād dhi trailokyaṃ prāptaṃ śakrādibhiḥ suraiḥ
english: By those who said, 'Following Kṛṣṇa may we conquer,' victory was won; for by his grace the three worlds were gained by Śakra and the other gods.

sanskrit: tasya te na vyathāṃ kāṃ cid iha paśyāmi bhārata yasya te jayam āśāste viśvabhuk tridaśeśvaraḥ
english: For you, O Bhārata, whose victory the all-consuming lord of the gods himself desires, I see no cause whatever for distress.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā svāṃ senāṃ samacodayat prativyūhann anīkāni bhīṣmasya bharatarṣabha
english: Saṃjaya said: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira urged on his own army, drawing up its divisions to counter those of Bhīṣma, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yathoddiṣṭāny anīkāni pratyavyūhanta pāṇḍavāḥ svargaṃ param abhīpsantaḥ suyuddhena kurūdvahāḥ
english: The Pāṇḍavas, those upholders of the Kuru line, arrayed their divisions as appointed, longing for the supreme heaven to be won through noble battle.

sanskrit: madhye śikhaṇḍino 'nīkaṃ rakṣitaṃ savyasācinā dhṛṣṭadyumnasya ca svayaṃ bhīmena paripālitam
english: In the centre, Śikhaṇḍin's division was guarded by Savyasācin, and that of Dhṛṣṭadyumna was protected by Bhīma himself.

sanskrit: anīkaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ rājan yuyudhānena pālitam śrīmatā sātvatāgryeṇa śakreṇeva dhanuṣmatā
english: The right wing, O king, was guarded by Yuyudhāna, the glorious foremost of the Sātvatas, like Śakra wielding the bow.

sanskrit: mahendrayānapratimaṃ rathaṃ tu; sopaskaraṃ hāṭakaratnacitram yudhiṣṭhiraḥ kāñcanabhāṇḍayoktraṃ; samāsthito nāgakulasya madhye
english: Yudhiṣṭhira mounted his chariot, like the very car of great Indra, furnished with all its equipment, bright with gold and gems, its harness and trappings of gold, taking his place in the midst of the host of elephants.

sanskrit: samucchritaṃ dāntaśalākam asya; supāṇḍuraṃ chatram atīva bhāti pradakṣiṇaṃ cainam upācaranti; maharṣayaḥ saṃstutibhir narendram
english: Held high above him, his snow-white parasol with ribs of ivory shone exceedingly fair, and the great sages, circling that lord of men reverently, attended him with hymns of praise.

sanskrit: purohitāḥ śatruvadhaṃ vadanto; maharṣivṛddhāḥ śrutavanta eva japyaiś ca mantraiś ca tathauṣadhībhiḥ; samantataḥ svasty ayanaṃ pracakruḥ
english: The household priests, aged great sages versed in sacred lore, pronouncing the doom of the foe, performed on every side the rites of benediction with muttered prayers, with sacred verses, and with healing herbs.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa vastrāṇi tathaiva gāś ca; phalāni puṣpāṇi tathaiva niṣkān kurūttamo brāhmaṇasān mahātmā; kurvan yayau śakra ivāmarebhyaḥ
english: Then that high-souled foremost of the Kurus, bestowing upon the brāhmaṇas garments and cattle, fruits and flowers and pieces of gold, went forth like Śakra among the immortals.

sanskrit: sahasrasūryaḥ śatakiṅkiṇīkaḥ; parārdhyajāmbūnadahemacitraḥ ratho 'rjunasyāgnir ivārcimālī; vibhrājate śvetahayaḥ sucakraḥ
english: Bright as a thousand suns, hung with a hundred little bells, adorned with the most precious river-born gold, the chariot of Arjuna, garlanded with flame like fire itself, blazed forth, drawn by white steeds and shod with goodly wheels.

sanskrit: tam āsthitaḥ keśavasaṃgṛhītaṃ; kapidhvajaṃ gāṇḍivabāṇahastaḥ dhanurdharo yasya samaḥ pṛthivyāṃ; na vidyate no bhavitā vā kadā cit
english: Mounted upon it, ape-bannered, the reins held by Keśava, with Gāṇḍīva and shafts in hand, stood the bowman whose equal on earth there is not, nor shall ever be at any time.

sanskrit: udvartayiṣyaṃs tava putrasenām; atīva raudraṃ sa bibharti rūpam anāyudho yaḥ subhujo bhujābhyāṃ; narāśvanāgān yudhi bhasma kuryāt
english: About to overthrow the army of your son, he wore a form most terrible—he who, fair-armed and weaponless, could with his bare arms reduce men, horses, and elephants to ashes in battle.

sanskrit: sa bhīmasenaḥ sahito yamābhyāṃ; vṛkodaro vīrarathasya goptā taṃ prekṣya mattarṣabhasiṃhakhelaṃ; loke mahendrapratimānakalpam
english: That Bhīmasena, Vṛkodara, together with the twins, was the guardian of the heroes' chariot-host; beholding him sporting like a maddened bull or a lion, peerless in the world and the equal of great Indra—

sanskrit: samīkṣya senāgragataṃ durāsadaṃ; pravivyathuḥ paṅkagatā ivoṣṭrāḥ vṛkodaraṃ vāraṇarājadarpaṃ; yodhās tvadīyā bhayavignasattvāḥ
english: —gazing upon Vṛkodara, unassailable, at the army's van, proud as a king of elephants, your warriors trembled, their spirits broken with fear, like camels mired in mud.

sanskrit: anīkamadhye tiṣṭhantaṃ rājaputraṃ durāsadam abravīd bharataśreṣṭhaṃ guḍākeśaṃ janārdanaḥ
english: Then Janārdana spoke to the prince standing in the midst of the army, the unassailable, the best of the Bhāratas, Guḍākeśa.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca ya eṣa goptā pratapan balastho; yo naḥ senāṃ siṃha ivekṣate ca sa eṣa bhīṣmaḥ kuruvaṃśaketur; yenāhṛtās triṃśato vājimedhāḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: This guardian, blazing in his strength, who eyes our army like a lion—this is Bhīṣma, the banner of the Kuru race, by whom thirty horse-sacrifices were performed.

sanskrit: etāny anīkāni mahānubhāvaṃ; gūhanti meghā iva gharmaraśmim etāni hatvā puruṣapravīra; kāṅkṣasva yuddhaṃ bharatarṣabheṇa
english: These divisions hide the mighty one as clouds conceal the hot-rayed sun. Having destroyed these, O foremost of men, then seek your battle with the bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca keṣāṃ prahṛṣṭās tatrāgre yodhā yudhyanti saṃjaya udagramanasaḥ ke 'tra ke vā dīnā vicetasaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: On which side, Saṃjaya, did the warriors at the front fight gladly? Who there were high of heart, and who were dispirited and bewildered?

sanskrit: ke pūrvaṃ prāharaṃs tatra yuddhe hṛdayakampane māmakāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ vā tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Who struck first there in that heart-shaking battle—my men or the Pāṇḍavas? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: kasya senāsamudaye gandhamālyasamudbhavaḥ vācaḥ pradakṣiṇāś caiva yodhānām abhigarjatām
english: In whose gathered army arose the fragrance of perfumes and garlands, and the auspicious words of the warriors as they roared aloud?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ubhayoḥ senayos tatra yodhā jahṛṣire mudā sragdhūpapānagandhānām ubhayatra samudbhavaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: In both armies there the warriors rejoiced with gladness, and on both sides arose the scents of garlands, incense, and drink.

sanskrit: saṃhatānām anīkānāṃ vyūḍhānāṃ bharatarṣabha saṃsarpatām udīrṇānāṃ vimardaḥ sumahān abhūt
english: As the close-massed, arrayed divisions, surging and swelling, crept forward, O bull of the Bhāratas, the clash between them grew immense.

sanskrit: vāditraśabdas tumulaḥ śaṅkhabherīvimiśritaḥ kuñjarāṇāṃ ca nadatāṃ sainyānāṃ ca prahṛṣyatām
english: Tumultuous was the din of the instruments, mingled with conches and kettledrums, with the trumpeting of elephants and the exultant shouts of the troops.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva kim akurvata saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: On the field of righteousness, on Kurukṣetra, gathered together and eager to fight, what did my men and the Pāṇḍavas do, O Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vyūḍhaṃ duryodhanas tadā ācāryam upasaṃgamya rājā vacanam abravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: But King Duryodhana, beholding the Pāṇḍava army drawn up in array, then approached his teacher and spoke these words.

sanskrit: paśyaitāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇām ācārya mahatīṃ camūm vyūḍhāṃ drupadaputreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā
english: Behold, O teacher, this mighty host of the sons of Pāṇḍu, arrayed by the son of Drupada, your wise disciple.

sanskrit: atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjunasamā yudhi yuyudhāno virāṭaś ca drupadaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: Here are heroes, mighty archers, equal in battle to Bhīma and Arjuna: Yuyudhāna and Virāṭa, and Drupada the great chariot-warrior;

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaketuś cekitānaḥ kāśirājaś ca vīryavān purujit kuntibhojaś ca śaibyaś ca narapuṃgavaḥ
english: Dhṛṣṭaketu, Cekitāna, and the valiant king of Kāśi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Śaibya, a bull among men;

sanskrit: yudhāmanyuś ca vikrānta uttamaujāś ca vīryavān saubhadro draupadeyāś ca sarva eva mahārathāḥ
english: Yudhāmanyu the bold, and the valiant Uttamaujas; the son of Subhadrā and the sons of Draupadī—all of them great chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye tān nibodha dvijottama nāyakā mama sainyasya saṃjñārthaṃ tān bravīmi te
english: But of our own who are the most distinguished, mark them, O best of the twice-born: the leaders of my army; for your knowledge I name them to you.

sanskrit: bhavān bhīṣmaś ca karṇaś ca kṛpaś ca samitiṃjayaḥ aśvatthāmā vikarṇaś ca saumadattis tathaiva ca
english: Your honoured self, and Bhīṣma, and Karṇa, and Kṛpa, ever victorious in battle; Aśvatthāman and Vikarṇa, and likewise the son of Somadatta;

sanskrit: anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ nānāśastrapraharaṇāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ
english: and many other heroes besides, who have laid down their lives for my sake, armed with manifold weapons, all skilled in war.

sanskrit: aparyāptaṃ tad asmākaṃ balaṃ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam paryāptaṃ tv idam eteṣāṃ balaṃ bhīmābhirakṣitam
english: Boundless is this force of ours, guarded by Bhīṣma, whereas the force of theirs, guarded by Bhīma, is limited.

sanskrit: ayaneṣu ca sarveṣu yathābhāgam avasthitāḥ bhīṣmam evābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi
english: Therefore, stationed each in his proper place at all the points of access, let all of you, every one, guard Bhīṣma above all.

sanskrit: tasya saṃjanayan harṣaṃ kuruvṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ siṃhanādaṃ vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān
english: Then, kindling his joy, the aged Kuru grandsire, the glorious one, roaring loud like a lion, blew his conch.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkhāś ca bheryaś ca paṇavānakagomukhāḥ sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdas tumulo 'bhavat
english: Thereupon conches and kettledrums, tabors and drums and horns were sounded all at once, and the noise of it was tumultuous.

sanskrit: tataḥ śvetair hayair yukte mahati syandane sthitau mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaś caiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ
english: Then, standing in their great chariot yoked with white steeds, Mādhava and the son of Pāṇḍu blew their divine conches.

sanskrit: pāñcajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ pauṇḍraṃ dadhmau mahāśaṅkhaṃ bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ
english: Hṛṣīkeśa blew Pāñcajanya, Dhanaṃjaya blew Devadatta, and Vṛkodara of dreadful deeds blew the great conch Pauṇḍra.

sanskrit: anantavijayaṃ rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca sughoṣamaṇipuṣpakau
english: King Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, blew Anantavijaya, and Nakula and Sahadeva blew Sughoṣa and Maṇipuṣpaka.

sanskrit: kāśyaś ca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaś ca sātyakiś cāparājitaḥ
english: The king of Kāśi, that supreme archer, and Śikhaṇḍin the great chariot-warrior, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Virāṭa, and the unvanquished Sātyaki;

sanskrit: drupado draupadeyāś ca sarvaśaḥ pṛthivīpate saubhadraś ca mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhān dadhmuḥ pṛthak pṛthak
english: Drupada and the sons of Draupadī, on every side, O lord of the earth, and the mighty-armed son of Subhadrā—each blew his several conch.

sanskrit: sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni vyadārayat nabhaś ca pṛthivīṃ caiva tumulo vyanunādayan
english: That tumultuous din, making sky and earth resound, rent the hearts of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons.

sanskrit: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ pravṛtte śastrasaṃpāte dhanur udyamya pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then, beholding Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons drawn up in their ranks, as the clash of weapons was about to begin, the ape-bannered son of Pāṇḍu raised his bow

sanskrit: hṛṣīkeśaṃ tadā vākyam idam āha mahīpate senayor ubhayor madhye rathaṃ sthāpaya me 'cyuta
english: and then spoke this word to Hṛṣīkeśa, O lord of the earth: 'Set my chariot, O Acyuta, between the two armies,

sanskrit: yāvad etān nirīkṣe 'haṃ yoddhukāmān avasthitān kair mayā saha yoddhavyam asmin raṇasamudyame
english: that I may look upon these who stand here eager for battle, and see with whom I must do combat in this enterprise of war.

sanskrit: yotsyamānān avekṣe 'haṃ ya ete 'tra samāgatāḥ dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddher yuddhe priyacikīrṣavaḥ
english: I would behold those who are gathered here ready to fight, seeking to do service in war to the evil-minded son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.'

sanskrit: evam ukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata senayor ubhayor madhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam
english: Thus addressed by Guḍākeśa, O Bhārata, Hṛṣīkeśa, having stationed that finest of chariots between the two armies

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇapramukhataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām uvāca pārtha paśyaitān samavetān kurūn iti
english: before Bhīṣma and Droṇa and all the lords of the earth, said: 'O Pārtha, behold these Kurus gathered together.'

sanskrit: tatrāpaśyat sthitān pārthaḥ pitṝn atha pitāmahān ācāryān mātulān bhrātṝn putrān pautrān sakhīṃs tathā
english: There the son of Pṛthā saw standing fathers and grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and comrades too;

sanskrit: śvaśurān suhṛdaś caiva senayor ubhayor api tān samīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvān bandhūn avasthitān
english: fathers-in-law and well-wishers as well, in both the armies. Beholding all these kinsmen arrayed there, the son of Kuntī

sanskrit: kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo viṣīdann idam abravīt dṛṣṭvemān svajanān kṛṣṇa yuyutsūn samavasthitān
english: was filled with deep compassion, and in dejection spoke this: 'Seeing these my own people, O Kṛṣṇa, drawn up and longing to fight,

sanskrit: sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati vepathuś ca śarīre me romaharṣaś ca jāyate
english: my limbs give way and my mouth grows parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvaṃ sraṃsate hastāt tvak caiva paridahyate na ca śaknomy avasthātuṃ bhramatīva ca me manaḥ
english: Gāṇḍīva slips from my hand, and my very skin is aflame; I cannot stand firm, and my mind seems to reel.

sanskrit: nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava na ca śreyo 'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanam āhave
english: And I behold omens of evil import, O Keśava; nor do I foresee any good in slaying my own kinsmen in battle.

sanskrit: na kāṅkṣe vijayaṃ kṛṣṇa na ca rājyaṃ sukhāni ca kiṃ no rājyena govinda kiṃ bhogair jīvitena vā
english: I crave not victory, O Kṛṣṇa, nor kingship, nor pleasures. What is kingship to us, O Govinda, what enjoyments, or even life itself?

sanskrit: yeṣām arthe kāṅkṣitaṃ no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca ta ime 'vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṃs tyaktvā dhanāni ca
english: Those for whose sake we desire kingship, enjoyments, and pleasures—these very ones stand here in battle, having renounced their lives and their wealth:

sanskrit: ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrās tathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ syālāḥ saṃbandhinas tathā
english: teachers, fathers, sons, and likewise grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and kinsmen besides.

sanskrit: etān na hantum icchāmi ghnato 'pi madhusūdana api trailokyarājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ nu mahīkṛte
english: These I would not wish to slay, O slayer of Madhu, even though they slay me—no, not for the sovereignty of the three worlds, how much less for the earth!

sanskrit: nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrān naḥ kā prītiḥ syāj janārdana pāpam evāśrayed asmān hatvaitān ātatāyinaḥ
english: By killing the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, what joy could be ours, O Janārdana? Only sin would cling to us were we to slay these, though they be aggressors.

sanskrit: tasmān nārhā vayaṃ hantuṃ dhārtarāṣṭrān sabāndhavān svajanaṃ hi kathaṃ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava
english: Therefore we ought not to slay the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra together with their kin; for having killed our own people, how could we be happy, O Mādhava?

sanskrit: yady apy ete na paśyanti lobhopahatacetasaḥ kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ mitradrohe ca pātakam
english: Even though these, their minds overcome by greed, see no fault in the ruin of the family, no crime in treachery to friends,

sanskrit: kathaṃ na jñeyam asmābhiḥ pāpād asmān nivartitum kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ prapaśyadbhir janārdana
english: how should we not know to turn back from this sin, O Janārdana, we who clearly see the fault in the ruin of the family?

sanskrit: kulakṣaye praṇaśyanti kuladharmāḥ sanātanāḥ dharme naṣṭe kulaṃ kṛtsnam adharmo 'bhibhavaty uta
english: In the ruin of the family, the eternal laws of the family perish; and when the law has perished, lawlessness overwhelms the whole family.

sanskrit: adharmābhibhavāt kṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kulastriyaḥ strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇasaṃkaraḥ
english: From the prevalence of lawlessness, O Kṛṣṇa, the women of the family are corrupted; and when the women are corrupted, O scion of Vṛṣṇi, there arises confusion of castes.
